title: The Sunny Acres Chore Chart
text:
Here is the chore chart for Sunny Acres Farm. Grandma hung it in the barn next to the {adjective} rooster calendar.

6:00 - Feed the chickens. Each one gets a scoop of corn and a handful of {plural noun}.
7:00 - Milk Daisy the cow. Sing to her {adverb}, or she will not stand still.
8:00 - Brush the horses. Bluebell likes her mane braided like a {noun}.
9:00 - Collect the eggs. Yesterday we found {number} eggs and one {noun}.
10:00 - Help Grandpa fix the fence. Bring the hammer, the nails, and the {adjective} {noun}.
11:00 - Give the pigs a bath. They love to {verb} in the mud right after.
12:00 - Lunch! Grandma is making soup with carrots, beans, and {plural noun}.

After chores, everyone gets lemonade on the porch. Grandma says we worked {adverb}. Grandpa says we worked like a team of {plural noun}.

title: A Letter to Mrs. Lopez
text:
Dear Mrs. Lopez,

I am spending the summer on my uncle's farm. It is very {adjective} here.

The farm has six cows, ten sheep, and a goat named Pepper. Pepper eats everything. Yesterday she ate a sock, a sunflower, and my uncle's {adjective} {noun}.

Every morning I help gather eggs. You have to reach under the hens {adverb} so they do not {verb}. My favorite hen is Lulu. She lays eggs that are a little bit {color}.

On Saturday we drove the tractor to town to buy seeds, flour, and a bag of {plural noun}. The tractor is very old. It sounds like a {animal} {verb ending in ing}. Everyone waved at us, and my uncle {past tense verb} back.

Please tell the class I said hello. I can now {verb} like a real farmer, and I can carry {number} buckets of {plural noun} at once.

Your student,
Noah

P.S. I am bringing you a jar of honey and a {noun}.

title: Meet the Animals at Maple Hill
text:
Welcome to Maple Hill Farm! Please follow the path and meet our animals.

Stop 1: The Cows. Bessie, Moo-Moo, and Gerald give us milk, cheese, and sometimes {plural noun}. Gerald is the {adjective} one.
Stop 2: The Pigs. Our pig, Waffles, can {verb} and count to {number}.
Stop 3: The Sheep. Their wool makes sweaters, blankets, and {adjective} socks.
Stop 4: The Duck Pond. Please do not feed the ducks any {food}. They like peas and {plural noun}.
Stop 5: The Barn Cat. Pumpkin sleeps {adverb} on a {noun} all day.
Stop 6: The Goat. Hold on to your {noun}. Our goat, Noodle, will try to eat it.

Before you leave, visit the gift shop. We sell honey, jam, and {adjective} {plural noun}. You can also take a photo with Farmer Joe, who will be {verb ending in ing} by the gate.

title: Grandma's Famous Farm Pie
text:
This is Grandma's famous Farm Pie. She makes it every summer for the county fair. She has won a ribbon {number} times.

You will need:
2 cups of flour
1 cup of sugar
3 fresh eggs
A big handful of {plural noun}
A pinch of {food}
1 {adjective} {noun}

First, mix the flour and sugar in a {adjective} bowl. Stir it {adverb} with a wooden spoon. Then crack the eggs and add a few {plural noun}. Grandma says the secret is to {verb} while you stir.

Ask a grown-up to bake the pie for one hour. When the kitchen smells like a {noun}, it is ready.

Let the pie cool on the windowsill. Last year a {animal} tried to sniff it, so Grandpa {past tense verb} on the porch all afternoon to guard it. Grandma says this year's pie is extra {adjective}.

title: The Barnyard News
text:
Good morning! This is Ellie, reporting live from Clover Farm for the Barnyard News.

Top story: Henrietta the hen laid an egg as big as a {noun}. Farmer Pat says it is the biggest egg she has ever seen. It is now resting on a {adjective} pillow in the kitchen.

In other news, the goats have learned how to {verb}. Nobody knows who taught them. They practice {adverb} behind the barn.

Weather: Sunny, with a chance of {plural noun} after lunch. Wear your {adjective} boots.

Sports: Yesterday the pigs had a race. Mud Pie won by {number} inches. He ran {adverb} and only stopped once to {verb}. The ducks {past tense verb} the whole time.

That is all for today. Next week we will visit the {adjective} sheep and ask them about their {plural noun}. Back to you, {name}!

title: Farmer Rosa's Garden Steps
text:
Planting a garden is easy. Just follow these steps from Farmer Rosa.

Step 1: Pick a sunny spot. Make sure the cows are not {verb ending in ing} on it.
Step 2: Dig a row of little holes. Each hole should be as deep as a {noun}.
Step 3: Drop two seeds into each hole. Some farmers also drop in a tiny {noun} for luck.
Step 4: Cover the seeds with dirt and pat them {adverb}.
Step 5: Water the garden every morning. Seeds also like it when you sing to them about {plural noun}.
Step 6: Wait {number} days. This is the hardest part. Try not to {verb}.
Step 7: Put up a scarecrow. Ours wears a {adjective} hat and holds a {noun}.

If you do everything right, you will grow carrots, beans, tomatoes, and a giant {adjective} {noun}. If a rabbit tries to {verb} in your garden, just say "{exclamation}!" and it will hop away.

title: The Barn Dance Is Saturday
text:
Attention, neighbors! The Hollow Creek Barn Dance is this Saturday night. Everyone is invited, even the {plural noun}.

The dance starts at {number} o'clock in the big red barn. Farmer Gus has swept the floor, hung lights from every {noun}, and taught the cows to {verb}.

The band will play fiddles, banjos, and a {adjective} washboard. Miss June will teach everyone the Chicken Shuffle. First you flap your arms, then you {verb}, then you spin around {adverb}. Last, you wiggle your {body part}.

There will be cornbread, apple cider, and a giant bowl of {food}. Please keep the goats away from the snack table. Last year they {past tense verb} right into the cupcakes and the {plural noun}.

Wear your boots and your most {adjective} hat. The best dancer wins a {noun} and gets to ride on the hay wagon first.

title: A Week on Aunt Molly's Farm
text:
Monday: Aunt Molly woke me up at five o'clock. The rooster was already {verb ending in ing} on the fence. I named the smallest chicken {name}.
Tuesday: I rode a pony named Peaches. She walks very {adverb} and stops to sniff every {noun}.
Wednesday: We picked strawberries. I ate {number} strawberries before they got to the basket.

Thursday: The pigs got out of their pen! We found them in the garden, sitting on a {adjective} {noun}.
Friday: Aunt Molly let me drive the tractor with her. It goes slower than a {animal}, but it felt {adjective}.
Saturday: We sold eggs and jam at the farmers market. A man bought six jars because they smelled like {plural noun}.

Sunday: I go home tomorrow. I will miss the {plural noun} so much. Aunt Molly gave me a jar of jam and a {noun} to take home. I told the cows I would {verb} for them every day until I come back.

title: Help Wanted at Willow Farm
text:
HELP WANTED at Willow Farm! Farmer Dan needs a helper for the summer. The job is hard work, but it is also very {adjective}.

Your jobs will include:
- Feeding the goats. They like hay, carrots, and {plural noun}.
- Counting the sheep. There should be {number} sheep. If there are more, one of them is probably a {noun}.
- Waking up the rooster. He sleeps late and gets {adjective} if you are too loud.
- Teaching the ducks how to {verb} across the yard.
- Brushing the horse's {body part} every night.

The best helper can {verb} {adverb} and does not mind a little mud.

You will be paid in fresh eggs, warm {plural noun}, and one {adjective} {noun} at the end of the summer. To sign up, knock on the barn door and say "{silly word}!" three times.

title: A Letter from Daisy the Cow
text:
Dear Farmer Ben,

Hello. It is me, Daisy, the cow in the third stall. I have a few requests.

First, the grass in the north field tastes a little bit like {plural noun}. Could we please eat in the south field instead?

Second, the barn radio is too loud. The chickens like to {verb} to it all night. Please turn it down or play something {adjective}.

Third, your new hat is very nice. It looks like a {noun}. When I showed the pigs, they {past tense verb} {adverb} for an hour.

Fourth, the barn cat keeps sleeping on my {noun}. Please ask her to nap on the {plural noun} instead.

Last, I would like a bigger bell. My cousin has one shaped like a {food}. It goes "{sound}!" every time she takes a step.

Thank you for the {adjective} hay. You are the best farmer in {place}.

Moo,
Daisy

P.S. The pigs say hello. They are {verb ending in ing} in the mud again.
